question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right as per the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid
Freedom of Speech and Expression
Right to Constitutional Remedies
Right to Equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid

Explanation:
Under the Constitution of India, Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35) include Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Freedom of Speech and Expression (Article 19(1)(a)), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid is mentioned under Article 39A, which is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), not a Fundamental Right. DPSPs are non-justiciable, while Fundamental Rights are justiciable. Thus, Option 1 is not a Fundamental Right.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid? → Article 39A
☛ Which Articles cover Right to Equality? → Articles 14-18
☛ Which Article covers Right to Constitutional Remedies? → Article 32
☛ Which Part contains Fundamental Rights? → Part III
☛ Which Part contains Directive Principles of State Policy? → Part IV
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुसार निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: समान न्याय और निःशुल्क कानूनी सहायता
बोलने और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता
संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार
समानता का अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है समान न्याय और निःशुल्क कानूनी सहायता

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में मौलिक अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 12-35) के अंतर्गत समानता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18), बोलने और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता (अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a)), और संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 32) शामिल हैं। समान न्याय और निःशुल्क कानूनी सहायता का उल्लेख अनुच्छेद 39A में किया गया है, जो राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) के अंतर्गत आता है, मौलिक अधिकार नहीं। DPSP गैर-न्यायोचित हैं, जबकि मौलिक अधिकार न्यायोचित होते हैं। इसलिए, विकल्प 1 मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है।

question: Which article deals with the formation of Finance Commission?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 279
Article 282
Article 281
Article 280
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 280

Explanation:
Article 280 of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of the Finance Commission. It empowers the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years or earlier if necessary. The Finance Commission's main role is to make recommendations on the distribution of taxes between the Union and States, grant-in-aid, and other matters related to financial relations. The Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, whose qualifications are prescribed by Parliament. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are not binding on the government but hold significant importance in fiscal policy formulation. Other options: Article 279 deals with calculation of tax distribution, Article 282 deals with expenditure under the Constitution, and Article 281 deals with the report of the Finance Commission.

☛ How many members does the Finance Commission have? → 5 members including Chairman
☛ What is the tenure of the Finance Commission? → 5 years
☛ What is the main function of the Finance Commission? → Recommendations on Centre-State financial relations
☛ Whom are the recommendations of the Finance Commission not binding on? → The government
question_hi: वित्त आयोग के गठन से संबंधित कौन सा अनुच्छेद है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)

Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 280

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 280 वित्त आयोग के गठन से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति को हर पांच वर्ष में या आवश्यकता होने पर पहले एक वित्त आयोग गठित करने का अधिकार देता है। वित्त आयोग का मुख्य कार्य केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच करों के वितरण, अनुदान सहायता और वित्तीय संबंधों से जुड़े मामलों पर सिफारिशें देना है। आयोग में एक अध्यक्ष और चार अन्य सदस्य होते हैं, जिनकी योग्यता संसद द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती है। वित्त आयोग की सिफारिशें सरकार के लिए बाध्यकारी नहीं होती हैं, परंतु वित्तीय नीति निर्माण में इनका महत्वपूर्ण स्थान होता है। अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 279 करों के वितरण की गणना, अनुच्छेद 282 संविधान के तहत व्यय, और अनुच्छेद 281 वित्त आयोग की रिपोर्ट से संबंधित है।

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is directed to establish right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 40
Article 42
Article 43
Article 41
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 41

Explanation:
Article 41 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to establish right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases. It is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which guide the government in policy-making. Under Article 41, the State is required to provide public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement. This article is based on socialist principles and aims to secure the socio-economic rights of citizens. Although it is non-justiciable, it holds significant importance for the welfare functions of the State. The provision emphasizes the State's role in ensuring a decent standard of living for its citizens.

☛ Article 41 is based on which principle → Socialist principles
☛ Article 41 is part of which Part → Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)
☛ Circumstances for public assistance under Article 41 → Unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement
☛ What type of right is Article 41 → Non-justiciable right

Explanation:

question: Which of the following schedules of the Indian Constitution enumerates the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states or union territories? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: First Schedule
Tenth Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Sixth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fourth Schedule

Explanation:
The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories. Under Article 80(2), the representation of states in the Rajya Sabha is based on their population. The Fourth Schedule explicitly lists the number of seats allotted to each state and union territory. For instance, Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of seats at 31. The First Schedule lists the territories of states and union territories, the Tenth Schedule pertains to anti-defection laws, and the Sixth Schedule deals with the administration of tribal areas. Therefore, the Fourth Schedule is the correct answer for Rajya Sabha seat allocation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Rajya Sabha seats for states → Fourth Schedule
☛ Article related to Rajya Sabha → Article 80
☛ State with most Rajya Sabha seats → Uttar Pradesh (31 seats)
☛ Territorial description of states → First Schedule
☛ Anti-defection law → Tenth Schedule
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी अनुसूची राज्यों या केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को राज्यसभा सीटों का आवंटन बताती है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: पहली अनुसूची
दसवीं अनुसूची
चौथी अनुसूची
छठी अनुसूची
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चौथी अनुसूची

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की चौथी अनुसूची राज्यसभा में राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को सीटों के आवंटन से संबंधित है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 80(2) के तहत राज्यसभा की सदस्य संख्या निर्धारित की जाती है, जिसमें राज्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व उनकी जनसंख्या के अनुपात में होता है। चौथी अनुसूची में प्रत्येक राज्य और केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए सीटों की संख्या स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लिखित है। उदाहरण के लिए, उत्तर प्रदेश को सबसे अधिक 31 सीटें आवंटित हैं। पहली अनुसूची राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के क्षेत्रों की सूची देती है, दसवीं अनुसूची दलबदल विरोधी कानून से संबंधित है, और छठी अनुसूची आदिवासी क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से जुड़ी है। इस प्रकार, राज्यसभा सीट आवंटन के लिए चौथी अनुसूची सही उत्तर है।

question: For how many years, from the commencement of the Indian Constitution, was English accepted as an associate language of the Union? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 5 years
20 years
10 years
15 years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15 years

Explanation:
When the Indian Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, Hindi was declared the official language of the Union. However, to accommodate non-Hindi speaking states, Article 343(2) and 343(3) allowed English to be used as an associate language for a period of 15 years. This period was to end in 1965. Due to strong anti-Hindi agitations, especially in Tamil Nadu, the Official Languages Act of 1963 provided for the continued use of English indefinitely. Today, English remains an associate official language of the Union.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Official language of Union → Hindi (Article 343)
☛ Initial period for English → 15 years (1950-1965)
☛ Official Languages Act → 1963, continued use of English
☛ Associate language of Union → English (Article 343(2))
☛ Anti-Hindi agitation → 1965 in Tamil Nadu

question: Which of the following politicians has never been a leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Shri Manmohan Singh
Shri Atal Bihari Bajpayee
Shri Pranab Mukherjee
Shri Narendra Modi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shri Manmohan Singh

Explanation:
The Leader of the House in Lok Sabha is a member of Parliament who leads the government's business in the house. Shri Manmohan Singh was never a member of Lok Sabha; he served as a member of Rajya Sabha and became Prime Minister. Hence, he could not become the Leader of the House in Lok Sabha. In contrast, Atal Bihari Vajpayee served as Leader of the House from 1998 to 2004, Pranab Mukherjee held the position from 2004 to 2012, and Narendra Modi has been the Leader of the House since 2014. According to the Indian Constitution, the Leader of the House must be a member of Lok Sabha. Since Manmohan Singh was from Rajya Sabha, he was ineligible.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which Prime Minister never became Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Manmohan Singh (he was from Rajya Sabha).
☛ Who served the longest as Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Pranab Mukherjee (2004-2012).
☛ Who is the current Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Narendra Modi.
☛ Can a Rajya Sabha member become Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → No, only Lok Sabha members.

question: In which of the following elections are one-third of the seats reserved for women? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/07/2021) Shift 2)

Legislative assembly

question: State emergency can be imposed in a state if it fails to run constitutionally. Who can declare state emergency? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: The President of India
The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Governor of the state
The Attorney General of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
Under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution, if a state fails to run according to constitutional machinery, the President of India can impose a state emergency (also known as President's Rule). The declaration is made by the President, not by the Governor or any other authority. The Governor can only submit a report to the President recommending such a step. Once the emergency is imposed, the executive and legislative powers of the state are transferred to the central government. This provision is part of Part XVIII of the Constitution. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months. State emergency can last for a maximum of three years, with periodic parliamentary approval every six months.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Who can revoke President's Rule? → President
☛ Maximum duration of state emergency? → 3 years (with approval every 6 months)

☛ Which amendment changed Article 356? → 44th Amendment
question_hi: यदि कोई राज्य संवैधानिक रूप से शासन करने में विफल रहता है, तो उस राज्य में आपातकाल की घोषणा की जा सकती है। राज्य आपातकाल की घोषणा कौन कर सकता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: There are different types of Bills introduced in the Lok Sabha. Which of the following is NOT one of them?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)
options: Revenue Bill
Financial Bills
Money Bills
Ordinary Bills
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Revenue Bill

Explanation:
In the Indian Parliament, three main types of Bills are introduced in the Lok Sabha: Ordinary Bills, Money Bills, and Financial Bills. A Revenue Bill is not a separate category; it is included under Financial Bills. Money Bills (Article 110) deal only with taxation, government expenditure, etc., and can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. Financial Bills (Article 117) contain financial matters other than those in Money Bills. Ordinary Bills deal with non-financial subjects. Hence, Revenue Bill is not an independent type of Bill in the Parliament.

question: As per Articles 344(1) and 351 of the Constitution of India, the eighth schedule includes the recognition of ____ languages.  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 2)
options: 23
22
26
20
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 22

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution currently recognizes 22 languages under Articles 344(1) and 351, which deal with the formation of the Official Language Commission and the development of Hindi. Initially, the Constitution listed 14 languages, but through amendments, the number increased. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi; the 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali; and the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, bringing the total to 22. These languages represent India's linguistic diversity and cultural heritage. The Eighth Schedule provides for the use of these languages in official purposes and promotes their development.

question: How can a new state be built in India?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)

It can be according to the Constitution
There is no provision in this regard in the Constitution
solution:

Explanation:
Under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament has the power to create new states. The process involves the President seeking the opinion of the concerned state legislature, but this opinion is not binding. Parliament can pass a bill by a simple majority to form a new state. The Constitution provides for reorganization of states, maintaining India's federal structure. The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 formed states on linguistic basis. Later, in 2000, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, and Jharkhand were created, and in 2014, Telangana was formed, all under Article 3.

question: What is the maximum number of members in the Lok Sabha? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 245
552
540
560
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 552

Explanation:
According to Article 81 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is fixed at 552 members. This includes 530 members representing the states, 20 members representing the Union Territories, and 2 members nominated by the President from the Anglo-Indian community. However, the 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) abolished the Anglo-Indian reservation, but the constitutional maximum limit remains 552. Currently, the effective strength is 543 (530+20+0 nominated). This limit ensures parliamentary representation and the democratic framework. The allocation is based on population and territorial representation, as per the Delimitation Commission orders.

question: By which word is the postponement of work done during the proceedings of Parliament? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Boycott
Termination
Suspension
Indefinitely postponement
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Suspension

Explanation:
During the proceedings of Parliament, the postponement of work is known as Suspension. It refers to temporarily halting the parliamentary proceedings for a specific period, after which the House resumes its sitting. A motion for suspension can be moved by any member and requires the approval of the House. Suspension is usually done when there is a need for discussion on a serious issue or to ensure smooth functioning of the House. This procedure is an important part of parliamentary proceedings as it allows for democratic debate and deliberation. Suspension differs from adjournment, which marks the end of a sitting. The Speaker or Chairperson plays a key role in managing the suspension process.

Explanation:
भारत में वर्तमान में कुल 8 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश हैं। ये हैं: अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीपसमूह, चंडीगढ़, दादरा और नगर हवेली और दमन और दीव, दिल्ली (राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र), जम्मू और कश्मीर, लद्दाख, लक्षद्वीप और पुदुचेरी। 2019 में जम्मू और कश्मीर का पुनर्गठन कर इसे केंद्र शासित प्रदेश बनाया गया, साथ ही लद्दाख को अलग केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का दर्जा मिला। दिल्ली और पुदुचेरी को विधान सभा वाले विशेष केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का दर्जा प्राप्त है। केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों का प्रशासन राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नियुक्त प्रशासक या उपराज्यपाल के माध्यम से किया जाता है।
